extracted.intended_audience: Texas Tribune journalists, editors, and readers interested in newsroom ethics and editorial standards
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial code for a state-level nonprofit newsroom that defines mission, story-selection criteria, reporting standards, and funder/firewall rules to guide nonpartisan, transparent, investigative journalism and public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: inform and engage Texans
rubrics_metrics.description: "Inform and engage Texans through in-depth investigations and reporting on public policy, politics, government, and statewide issues."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote civic engagement through original, explanatory journalism and public events; mission shapes coverage priorities and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions made by journalists alone, not influenced by donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donations do not entitle preferential treatment or protection from scrutiny; maintain an editorial firewall between funding and newsroom decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "There are no sacred cows; we aggressively pursue all stories we deem newsworthy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to investigate powerful actors and institutions; prioritize watchdog work even when subjects are influential or well-connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truthful, transparent, respectful reporting; facts accurate, complete, fairly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy and completeness; make sourcing and methods clear where possible; present context fairly and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective journalism distinguishes the Tribune in a polarized media universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories without partisan bias; pursue facts and explanations rather than advancing political agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Priority: public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize coverage of public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reporting on policy issues that have statewide import and affect Texans broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Priority: politics and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize coverage of politics and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover political institutions, actors, processes, and decisions that shape public life at the state level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Priority: statewide issues (not micro-local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize statewide issues rather than micro-local stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor stories with broad relevance across Texas rather than narrowly localized items, unless local stories have wider policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Priority: issues affecting Texans broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize issues that affect Texans broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select stories with significant impact or relevance to large segments of the state's population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: civic significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a story has civic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stories that matter to public life, government accountability, or citizens' ability to participate in civic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: educational value (explanatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a story has educational/explanatory value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor reporting that helps readers understand complex policy, political processes, or government functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: original reporting (vs. aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer original reporting over aggregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value reporting that produces new information, documents, or analysis rather than merely rehashing others' coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: watchdog potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Select stories with watchdog potential — "no sacred cows."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose investigations that hold power to account, reveal wrongdoing, or expose systemic problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: transparency-supportable (sources nameable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor stories where transparency can be supported (sources nameable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reporting that can be documented and attributed; ensure claims are supportable by nameable sources when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Selection Test: nonpartisan framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Require nonpartisan framing in story selection and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame issues and evidence neutrally to avoid taking partisan positions; clearly separate reporting from opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Quality Marker: in-depth investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce in-depth investigative reporting as a marker of quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest sufficient time and resources for deep reporting, document review, and analysis to produce substantive, original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Quality Marker: public-facing data tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use public-facing data tools as part of distinctive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and publish data-driven tools and visualizations that enable public understanding and use of reporting findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Quality Marker: live events as journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat live events (public events) as a form of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use events to inform and engage the public, integrating reporting and public conversation as part of editorial output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Quality Marker: newsletter-driven engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use newsletters to drive public-facing engagement and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage email newsletters to explain reporting, reach audiences, and foster ongoing civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding: acceptable funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: List of funding mechanisms: membership programs, major donations, foundation support, corporate sponsorships (clearly labeled), events, paid newsletters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversified funding supports nonprofit journalism; specific source types must be handled transparently and labeled appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding practice: disclosure of major donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Major donations are disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly disclose significant gifts to maintain trust and allow readers to assess potential influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding practice: corporate sponsorship labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate sponsorships must be clearly labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sponsored content and partnerships conspicuously so audiences can distinguish editorial content from sponsored material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder firewall
rubrics_metrics.description: Funder firewall ensures editorial independence regardless of source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain formal and practical separation between fundraising activities and newsroom decision-making to prevent donor influence on coverage.
